findings.title: [P1] Unsubscribe the message listener in unmount
findings.body: `mount()` now registers an inline anonymous closure (`socket.on("message", message => this.render(message))`, `src/socket-view.ts:14`), so the handler reference is unrecoverable, and `unmount()` (`src/socket-view.ts:18`) only sets `this.socket = undefined` without detaching. Any socket that outlives the view keeps invoking `render()` on an unmounted view after `unmount()` returns, and each mount/unmount cycle permanently adds another listener that retains the `SocketView` instance (duplicate renders plus a growing memory leak). The removed code (`this.socket?.off("message", this.onMessage)`) established exactly this teardown contract, so the regression occurs in the component's primary lifecycle flow, not an edge case. Restore a stored handler (or capture the closure) and call `socket.off("message", handler)` in `unmount()`.
